newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND, ITALY CLOSER TO DEBT ECOCONVERSION DEAL.
newsitem.headline: POLAND, ITALY CLOSER TO DEBT ECOCONVERSION DEAL.

text.p: Poland and Italy reached an initial deal on Friday on writing-off part of Warsaw's $1.6-billion debt to the Italian government which is to be used for environment protection schemes.
"We have convinced the Italian side that it is worthwhile to get engaged in ecoconversion," Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said after talks with Italian Foreign Trade Minister Augusto Fantozzi.
He said it was too early to name the sum involved before talks with Italy's treasury ministry but that theoretically up to $160 million could be written off.

Under Poland's debt-relief agreement with its government creditors, grouped in the so-called Paris club, up to 10 percent of Warsaw's liabilities could be written off if the same amounts were spent on environmental projects, he said.
"But we have not discussed the sum," he said.

Kaczmarek added the two countries overcame many differences over trade issues such as Italian barriers to Poland's exports of livestock and animal skin and Poland's recognition of Italy's quality certificates.
Italy also accepted Poland's regulations under which South Korea's Daewoo conglomerate is exempted from duty on import of car parts brought for assembly in Poland.
Daewoo is a major competitor of Italy's Fiat , which produces and assembles cars at its Polish unit.
Fantozzi reiterated his government's support for Poland's efforts for join the European Union and NATO.
